required_changes: Page-order inversion: a marked break outside a rubric can now be moved past a marked break inside a rubric. Example: `<tei:p>…</tei:p><pb N/><tei:note type="instruction">words <pb N+1/> more</tei:note><tei:p>prayer</tei:p>`. pb N still skips the rubric's non-running words (`_next_words` → `_first_words` → `_running`, which excludes every tei:note) and is moved into the prayer paragraph. pb N+1 is now a candidate and stays inside the rubric (`_rubric_words_follow`). The output then sets link N+1 before link N. Before the fix this couldn't happen, because pb N+1 was never a candidate. `_unmark_if_empty_page` doesn't catch it because the two breaks aren't siblings. Prevent it: when the search for words would cross a marked candidate break, keep the moving break before that rubric (or leave it in place). Add a scan_links unit test for this case. Since a page that begins with a rubric is the situation this fix targets, this case is likely, not a corner case.

Add a test showing that a rubric break only now counted as a candidate does not change which breaks are chosen elsewhere. A rubric break with printing tokens in `@ed` now adds to `editions[edition]` (the set `_choose` checks units against). It can also become the `earlier` break `_context` returns for a later enclosing or child group. Either can change which printing a later group links. Test a rubric `<pb ed="<edition> <path>">` before a transclusion whose group has several printings and no unit context, so the outcome is pinned. If the intended behaviour is that rubric breaks never act as `earlier` context, encode that rule.

notes: Candidate selection is correct as written. A break is skipped if any ancestor is a non-rubric tei:note, a tei:standOff or a tei:teiHeader, so a rubric nested inside commentary or standOff stays excluded, and the new test covers both cases. A rubric nested inside a rubric is allowed.

Text/tail handling in `_rubric_words_follow` is sound. For text it walks up from the element, for a tail from its parent, stops at the nearest rubric ancestor, and gives up when it reaches head, label or a non-rubric note first. So commentary words inside a rubric don't keep the break, and the test covers that. One edge case: a break inside a tei:head or tei:label within a rubric stays in place if rubric words come later, even though it sits in the head. That's acceptable but untested.

The break at the end of a rubric still goes through `_next_words`, and the walk climbs out of the note to the next running words, as tested. Breaks outside a rubric behave as before, apart from the inversion described in required_changes.

Columns and parallel text: a rubric break that stays in place never consults `_Columns`, so it stays in its own column. No test puts a rubric break inside p:parallelItem, or a rubric break at the end of a column whose words are in the column's next block. Consider one parallel-text test for each case.

Cross-language: there's no test where the Hebrew and English columns each have a break inside a rubric at different positions. Breaks inside rubrics that stay in place aren't aligned to milestones, which is consistent with the existing rule that only the break's own column is searched.
The PDF and HTML tests check the exact output position: `before \OSScanLink{…}after`, and in HTML a link whose tail is 'after'. That's good end-to-end coverage for the instruction case.

Minor: the module docstring ("A marked break is then moved forward to just before the next words…") doesn't mention the rubric exception. Add a sentence so it stays the single description of the rule.
